answers.solution:
(a) Progress in life depends a good deal on crossing one threshold after another, that is, on overcoming one difficulty after another.

(b) We can accomplish the most difficult tasks by hard work and genuine effort. Like the little boy who at last wrote his name with ease, we must accept each challenge and be determined to cross it, as we have crossed many thresholds before.

(c) When a new difficulty obstructs our path, we should not complain. We should accept the challenge and be determined to cross this threshold as we have crossed others in the past.

(d) Real progress stops when people steer clear of thresholds: they avoid anything that needs real thinking and energy, stay in a rut and make no effort to seek new obstacles to overcome.

(e) De Morgan's life teaches us that it is never too late to begin something new. He started writing novels after he was sixty, which shows that a man can go on learning throughout life.

(f) It means that we should never rest after reaching one goal. Once one dream is achieved, we should aim at a still higher and nobler dream.

(g) He made a success of his new business, even though he started it after middle life.

(h) Middle aged and elderly people add brilliance to their lives by continuing to cross thresholds, that is, by taking up new challenges such as a new business or a new skill.

(j) We should always steer clear of bad company. ('Steer clear of' means to keep away from.)

(k) rut (the passage says some people 'prefer to stay in a rut', meaning a fixed, dull habit or routine).
answers.finalAnswer: on crossing one threshold (difficulty) after another; by hard work and genuine effort, accepting each challenge with determination; not complain but accept the challenge and determine to cross it; avoiding thresholds and staying in a rut without effort; that it is never too late to start something new, since man can learn all his life; never to rest after one achievement but keep aiming at a still higher goal; he made a success of it; by continuing to cross thresholds and taking up new challenges; We should steer clear of bad company.; rut

A suitable title is 'A Morning View' (or 'The View from My Window').

The whole poem describes what a man sees when he pulls back his curtains one morning: a butterfly in the sunny garden and two laughing girls on the sidewalk.

Two poetic devices used in the poem are:

1. Simile: 'As the cadence of their laughter, / Waved in the air like Tunisian silk.' The rhythm of the girls' laughter is compared to silk waving in the air, using the word 'like'.

2. Alliteration: 'red and radiant'. The 'r' sound is repeated at the start of words close together.

(Other examples: personification in 'a laughing sidewalk', and inversion in 'A turquoise skirt wore the one'.)
answers.finalAnswer: Simile: the cadence of their laughter waved in the air like Tunisian silk; Alliteration: red and radiant

answers.solution: The poem shows that happiness lies in the simple sights of everyday life. One morning a man opens his curtains and sees a bright orange butterfly in his sunny garden and two cheerful girls walking and laughing on the sidewalk. He does not need grand scenes of harvests or mountains on a screen; these small, natural moments of beauty and joy are enough to brighten his day.
answers.finalAnswer: Simple everyday sights seen from a window, a butterfly and two laughing girls, can fill an ordinary morning with joy, more than grand scenes on a screen.

The simile is used in the line 'Waved in the air like Tunisian silk'. The soft, flowing sound (cadence) of the two maidens' laughter is compared to fine Tunisian silk waving in the air, to show how light and pleasant their laughter was.

Essays written on (b), (c) and (d).

(b) The Value of Friendship

A friend is one of the greatest gifts life can give us. A true friend shares our joys and stands beside us in our sorrows. When we are happy, a friend doubles our happiness, and when we are sad, a friend makes our sadness lighter. There is a saying, 'A friend in need is a friend indeed.' Such a friend tells us the truth even when it is bitter and stops us from going the wrong way. Good friends help us to study, to play and to grow into better people. However, we must choose our friends with care, because bad company can spoil our habits. Friendship also asks something from us: loyalty, honesty and trust. If we are good friends to others, we will never be lonely in life.

(c) The Role of Students in Bringing About a Welcome Change in Our Environment

Our environment is in danger today. The air and water are polluted, trees are being cut down and plastic waste lies everywhere. Students can play a big role in bringing about a welcome change. First, they can begin at home and at school by switching off fans and lights when they are not needed, saving water and saying no to plastic bags. Secondly, they can plant trees on their birthdays and look after them. Thirdly, they can form eco-clubs, keep their school campus clean and hold awareness rallies in their locality. Children can also teach their parents and neighbours to separate wet and dry waste. Students are the citizens of tomorrow. If they form good habits now, our country will surely become cleaner and greener.

(d) Every Dark Cloud Has a Silver Lining

This proverb means that even in the worst situation there is some hope or some good. A dark cloud stands for trouble and sorrow, and its bright silver edge stands for the hope hidden behind it. Life is full of ups and downs. When we fail in an examination, we feel sad, but the failure shows us our weak points and teaches us to work harder. Many great people faced hard times before they became successful. Thomas Edison failed many times before he made the electric bulb, yet every failure taught him something new. An illness, too, teaches us the value of good health. So we should never lose hope in bad times. We must stay calm, be patient and keep trying, because bad days do not last forever.

Rahul's Presence of Mind

Rahul was alone at home. Suddenly the phone rang. He picked up the receiver and a man's voice said, 'Hello, I am calling from the bank. Your father's account will be closed today. Please tell me the number on his ATM card and its secret PIN at once.'

Rahul was only twelve, but he remembered what his teacher had told the class: a bank never asks for such details on the phone. He kept calm and said, 'Uncle, my father has gone out. Please call again after half an hour.'

At once he rang up his father at the office and told him everything. His father praised him and informed the bank and the police cyber cell. When the man called again, Rahul kept him talking, just as the police had told him. The call was traced, and that very evening the police arrested the cheat, who had robbed many people in the same way.

A few days later the Inspector visited Rahul's school and gave him a certificate for his courage and presence of mind. Rahul had learnt that a calm mind is the best weapon in times of danger.

Subject: Complaint against the use of loudspeakers

Sir,

I wish to bring to your notice the nuisance of loudspeakers in our colony. Although the government has banned the use of loudspeakers, they are still played at full volume at functions, parties and shops till late at night.

I am a student preparing for an important examination. The loud noise makes it impossible for me to concentrate on my studies. Old people and patients in our area are also badly disturbed, and many cannot sleep at night.

I request you to take strict action against those who break the law. Regular checking by the police in our area will surely stop this nuisance.

I shall be very grateful to you.

Yours faithfully
A.B.C.

Title: The Noble Teacher

Teaching is the most honourable profession because the teacher shapes the character of children. Besides training their minds, he teaches them good citizenship, cleanliness, polite speech and good manners. He can do this only if he himself lives a simple, pure and disciplined life. A teacher also stays young at heart. Constant company of cheerful young pupils keeps him happy and helps him forget his passing household worries.

(a) One of the reasons for his failure is his careless attitude.
('One of' takes a plural noun.)

(b) He need not go there. (or: He does not need to go there.)
(As a modal, 'need' takes no 's' and no 'to'.)

(c) Delhi Capitals would have won IPL 2019 if they had played well.
(The 'if' clause takes the past perfect, not 'would have'.)

(d) The number of people we need to hire is thirteen.
('The number' is singular.)

(e) If you freeze water, it becomes a solid.
(A scientific fact takes the simple present in both clauses.)
answers.finalAnswer: One of the reasons for his failure is his careless attitude.; He need not go there.; Delhi Capitals would have won IPL 2019 if they had played well.; The number of people we need to hire is thirteen.; If you freeze water, it becomes a solid.
